analyst_view.overall: Early view: a relegation six-pointer between two clubs from the Valencia region, one point apart: Levante (17th) got out of the bottom three with a 0-0 at Celta thanks to seven saves from Mathew Ryan, and Elche (18th) are bottom-three after losing 2-0 at home to Betis. Elche are much stronger away (9 of their 10 points) than at home, but Martín Anselmi has a list of knocks in midfield. Luis Castro wants Levante more patient on the ball.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. With so much at stake, neither coach wants an open game: Levante sat deep and played for the point at Celta, and Anselmi said before the Betis game that he does not want end-to-end matches. Elche's away games have included a 0-0 at Villarreal, so I lean lower.

corners.text: The site expects 8.9 corners. Elche like the ball and won nine corners even while losing to Betis, while Levante took one corner at Celta and defend deep. If Elche have most of the ball, their corner count should push the total up.

cards.text: The model has 4.4 cards. A relegation game between regional rivals usually has more fouls, and Elche took four yellows against Betis. Five cards looks closer than four.

shots.text: The site expects 29.7 shots. Levante had only six shots at Celta and Elche 13 against Betis, and nerves make games like this cautious. Mid-20s is more realistic.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 on target. Elche failed to score from 13 shots against Betis, and with Lemar, Aguado and possibly Ali Houary missing they lack a midfielder who makes chances. Seven looks right.
